breadcrumbTitle: How to Assemble a Tiled Poster
title: How to Print, Trim & Glue a Multi-Page Poster Cleanly
description: Step-by-step illustrated guide to printing tiled posters at 100% scale, trimming borders, aligning (+) crosshairs, and gluing sheets cleanly.
h1: How to Print, Trim & Glue a Multi-Page Poster
lead: Follow this quick drafting workflow to assemble multi-page A4 or US Letter tiles with invisible seams, zero stair-stepping, and exact dimensions.

sections.heading: Step 1: Print Page 1 First & Measure the Calibration Ruler
paragraphs: Every multi-page PDF generated by WidePosterMaker starts with an Assembly Map page showing a miniature grid (A1, A2, B1...) alongside exact 50 mm and 2.0 inch calibration bars.

Before wasting 12 or 20 sheets of paper, print Page 1 alone and verify with a real ruler that 50 mm measures 50 mm (and 2.0 in measures 2.0 in). If it prints smaller (for example 47 mm), your PDF viewer applied 'Fit to printable area'. Switch the print scale setting to 'Actual Size' or '100%'.

sections.heading: Step 2: Trim Only Top & Left Margins on Overlapping Sheets
paragraphs: The fastest mistake to avoid is trimming all four sides of every sheet. Instead, keep the right and bottom overlap tabs intact (marked with dashed blue lines and neighbor arrows like '-> A2' or 'v B1'), and only trim:
list: Column 1 sheets (A1, B1, C1): keep left edge trimmed cleanly to the poster border if mounting frameless, and leave the right glue tab intact.
Interior sheets (A2, B2, etc.): trim the TOP and LEFT white printer margins directly through the corner crop ticks.
Last column and bottom row sheets: trim outer excess margins as desired after assembly or before.

sections.heading: Step 3: Glue Row by Row Using (+) Crosshairs
paragraphs: Assemble complete horizontal rows first (A1 + A2 + A3), then join completed rows vertically (Row A + Row B). Using a dry solid glue stick instead of wet liquid glue prevents paper wrinkling along the seam.
list: Use a metal straightedge and craft knife (or paper guillotine) rather than scissors for dead-straight seams.
Dry-fit two sheets over a bright window or lamp if aligning dark artwork — the (+) crosshairs lock into exact alignment.
Press seams flat under a heavy book for 10 minutes before hanging or framing.

faqs.q: Should I use glue stick, double-sided tape, or liquid glue?
faqs.a: A solid glue stick or thin double-sided tape (or masking tape on the reverse side for patterns) keeps paper flat without water-induced wrinkling.

faqs.q: Why do WidePosterMaker tiles only put overlap tabs on the right and bottom?
faqs.a: One-sided tabs guarantee consistent overlapping direction (left-to-right, top-to-bottom), cutting trimming work in half compared to four-sided borders.

faqs.q: How wide should I set the glue overlap?
faqs.a: 10 mm (about 3/8 inch) works well for most posters and patterns. Use 15 mm for very large wall banners or 5 mm if maximizing usable print width per sheet.
